claims.title: Customer order details may be readable between the customer and mobile app
claims.description: If `flow:entity:customer>process:mobile-app>browse-and-order` is not protected in transit, an attacker able to observe the customer-device path can intercept browsing activity and order details before they reach `process:mobile-app`. The `encryption_in_transit` state is unknown, so this is conditional rather than an assertion of plaintext. The disclosed order information can be correlated with the customer data subsequently sent to `process:web-api`.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `flow:entity:customer>process:mobile-app>browse-and-order` has unstated transport encryption, while an attacker still needs a position on the customer-device path. Impact is medium because the flow carries PII-bearing browsing and order details to `process:mobile-app`.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce protected customer-to-app transport
mitigations.detail: Establish the transport posture for `flow:entity:customer>process:mobile-app>browse-and-order` and require authenticated TLS for any network hop carrying order details.

claims.title: Customer details are readable on the plaintext mobile-app API connection
claims.description: An attacker able to observe the boundary-crossing `flow:process:mobile-app>process:web-api>api-traffic` can intercept customer order-placement traffic because its transport encryption is stated absent. The HTTP flow carries customer details from `process:mobile-app` into internet-facing `process:web-api`; captured details can be used to identify and target customers whose records are then retained through `flow:process:web-api>store:user-database>customer-records`.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because the flow crosses from `boundary:customer-device` to Sokify systems and passive capture needs only path access, not an application credential. Impact is high because the plaintext flow carries PII to `process:web-api`, which handles PII and financial customer records.

mitigations.detail: Set `encryption_in_transit` for `flow:process:mobile-app>process:web-api>api-traffic` to TLS 1.2+ and validate the API certificate in `process:mobile-app`; use HTTPS exclusively.

mitigations.summary: Minimize sensitive order fields in requests
mitigations.detail: Use opaque references where possible so the API request contains only the fields necessary to place the order.

claims.title: Catalogue SQL statements may be observable crossing from Marketing to the API
claims.description: If `flow:process:catalogue-spreadsheet>process:web-api>sql-statements` lacks transport protection, a network observer between the marketing-office zone and `process:web-api` can intercept SQL statements that reveal catalogue prices and product-copy changes. This flow is a decided boundary crossing, but `encryption_in_transit` is unknown; the claim is conditional on that control being absent. The disclosed commercial changes can enable a competitor or insider to anticipate catalogue updates before they are published.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional: the Marketing-to-API flow crosses a trust boundary, but its transport encryption is unstated and the attacker needs network-path access. Impact is medium because the SQL statements disclose business-critical price and product-copy changes handled by `process:web-api`.

mitigations.detail: Use mutually authenticated TLS or a protected API protocol for `flow:process:catalogue-spreadsheet>process:web-api>sql-statements` rather than an unstated transport.

claims.title: Customer database traffic may expose card and address data inside Sokify systems
claims.description: If `flow:process:web-api>store:user-database>customer-records` is unencrypted in transit, an attacker with a foothold on the internal path can intercept the customer names, addresses, and payment-card information exchanged between `process:web-api` and `store:user-database`. `encryption_in_transit` is unknown, so this is a conditional transport-disclosure finding, not a claim that the internal channel is plaintext. The capture can reveal the same confidential corpus that the API keeps in the database and support targeted fraud against customers.

quotes.text:
The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card
they paid with.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the encryption state of the intra-zone database flow is unstated and interception requires an internal network foothold. Impact is high because `store:user-database` is confidential and holds PII and financial card information.

mitigations.summary: Require authenticated encryption on the database connection
mitigations.detail: Verify the current setting, then require TLS for `flow:process:web-api>store:user-database>customer-records` and authenticate the database endpoint to the API.

claims.title: Order handover to SIMS may disclose delivery details on an unverified internal link
claims.description: If `flow:process:web-api>process:sims>order-handover` is not encrypted, an attacker able to observe the internal handover can intercept placed-order data, including delivery addresses and the number stored against the order. The flow's `encryption_in_transit` attribute is unknown, so the threat is conditional. That information enables targeted contact with customers and identifies the data later sent to `process:fax-gateway`.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the handover remains within the Sokify zone and requires an internal observation position, while its encryption state is unstated. Impact is medium because the order handover includes customer delivery addresses and telephone-number information.

mitigations.detail: Establish whether `flow:process:web-api>process:sims>order-handover` uses protected transport and require mTLS or equivalent encryption for order payloads.

claims.title: Delivery addresses may be exposed while SIMS writes the flat file
claims.description: If transport on `flow:process:sims>store:delivery-address-flat-file>address-write` is unencrypted, an attacker with access to the local or internal path can intercept delivery addresses as `process:sims` writes them to `store:delivery-address-flat-file`. The transport control is unknown, so this is conditional and requires verification rather than assuming cleartext. Captured addresses can be correlated with dispatch information sent onward through `flow:process:sims>process:fax-gateway>dispatch-note`.

quotes.text:
It writes the delivery address into a flat
file kept alongside it — only addresses go in that file, nothing else

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because an attacker needs an internal or local observation position and encryption on this flow is unstated. Impact is medium because `store:delivery-address-flat-file` is confidential and holds customer PII addresses.

mitigations.detail: Determine how `process:sims` reaches `store:delivery-address-flat-file` and encrypt or isolate the path when it is not a strictly local protected filesystem operation.

claims.title: Dispatch notes may be readable between SIMS and the fax gateway
claims.description: If `flow:process:sims>process:fax-gateway>dispatch-note` lacks encryption in transit, an internal on-path attacker can intercept dispatch notes carrying customer names and addresses before `process:fax-gateway` sends the confirmation fax. The encryption state is unknown, so the disclosure is conditional. The attacker can use the disclosed identity and delivery information to target the same customer outside the application.

quotes.text:
it
sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway, which faxes the customer a
confirmation with their name and address on it.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the SIMS-to-fax-gateway connection is internal and its encryption is unstated, so interception requires a prior internal position. Impact is medium because the dispatch note carries customer names and addresses, which are PII.

mitigations.detail: Verify `flow:process:sims>process:fax-gateway>dispatch-note` transport protection and use authenticated encryption between SIMS and the fax gateway.

claims.title: Fax confirmation contents may be observable in transit to the customer
claims.description: If the fax leg `flow:process:fax-gateway>entity:customer>confirmation-fax` is not protected against interception, an attacker able to observe that delivery can read the customer's name and address from the confirmation. This is conditional because `encryption_in_transit` is unknown, although the flow crosses from Sokify systems to the customer-device zone. The disclosed identity and address enable targeted social engineering against the recipient.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the fax confirmation crosses from Sokify systems to the customer zone and an attacker needs a delivery-path observation position, while encryption is unstated. Impact is medium because the confirmation carries the customer's name and address.

mitigations.summary: Replace or protect the customer confirmation channel
mitigations.detail: Do not transmit customer PII over an unverified fax path; use an authenticated encrypted customer channel, or minimize the fax content to a non-sensitive reference.

claims.title: An unintended fax recipient can read customer confirmation details
claims.description: `flow:process:fax-gateway>entity:customer>confirmation-fax` sends a confirmation containing the customer's name and address, but destination verification is stated absent. A person who receives a fax sent to an incorrect, reassigned, or otherwise unintended number can read those details directly from the fax. This is a recipient-verification disclosure distinct from transport interception: it lands the message with the wrong recipient even if its transit path is otherwise protected. The recipient can use the identity and address to target the affected customer.

quotes.text:
The gateway dials the
number stored against the order and nobody checks it arrived at the right
place.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because destination verification is stated absent, although a wrong or reassigned destination must exist for an unintended recipient to receive the fax. Impact is medium because the fax exposes the customer's name and address.

mitigations.summary: Verify the intended recipient before disclosing PII
mitigations.detail: Replace the unauthenticated fax confirmation with a recipient-authenticated channel, or require an out-of-band verification step before sending any confirmation containing name or address.
If fax remains temporarily necessary, send only an opaque order reference and require the customer to authenticate to retrieve personal details.

claims.title: A storage copy may expose all customer records if the user database lacks at-rest encryption
claims.description: `store:user-database` is confidential and holds customer names, addresses, and payment-card information, but its `encryption_at_rest` attribute is unknown. If that unknown resolves to no encryption at rest, an attacker who obtains a disk, snapshot, backup, or decommissioned storage copy can read the customer-record corpus without using `process:web-api` or its normal database flow. This is conditional on the unresolved at-rest control, not an assertion that the database is currently unencrypted. The resulting card and identity data can enable customer-targeted fraud.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the store's at-rest encryption is unstated and obtaining an operational storage copy is a prerequisite. Impact is high because `store:user-database` is confidential and contains both PII and financial card data for the customer corpus.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce encryption for database storage and copies
mitigations.detail: Establish the at-rest state of `store:user-database`, then require KMS-managed encryption for the primary store, backups, snapshots, and decommissioned media, with tightly scoped key access.
Tokenize payment-card data and retain only the minimum payment reference necessary for orders.

claims.title: A storage copy may expose delivery addresses if the flat file lacks at-rest encryption
claims.description: `store:delivery-address-flat-file` is a confidential PII store, but `encryption_at_rest` is unknown. If the file is stored without at-rest encryption, a person who obtains its host volume, backup, copied file, or decommissioned media can read delivery addresses directly without authenticating to `process:sims`. This is conditional on the unresolved encryption state. The addresses can be combined with names disclosed through confirmation or dispatch flows to target customers at their homes.

quotes.text: only addresses go in that file, nothing else

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because at-rest protection for `store:delivery-address-flat-file` is unstated and a storage copy must be obtained. Impact is medium because the store is confidential and contains customer delivery-address PII.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the flat file and its operational copies
mitigations.detail: Determine the at-rest protection for `store:delivery-address-flat-file` and require managed encryption and restrictive filesystem, backup, and decommissioning controls for the file and every copy.

claims.title: An unauthenticated API caller may elicit customer records through the web API
claims.description: `process:web-api` is internet-facing and reads and writes `store:user-database` through `flow:process:web-api>store:user-database>customer-records`, which carries customer names, addresses, and payment-card information. Authentication for the database flow and the API's authentication mechanism are both unstated. If `process:web-api` does not enforce authenticated, object-scoped read authorization, an outside caller can send requests that elicit another customer's records through the API rather than accessing the store directly. This is conditional on those unresolved controls; it is not an assertion that anonymous reads are accepted. Successful responses disclose the customer corpus exposed by the API's read path and enable targeted fraud.

quotes.text:
The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card
they paid with.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `process:web-api` is internet-facing while its authentication mechanism and the database-flow authentication are unstated. Impact is high because elicited responses can expose confidential PII and financial card data held in `store:user-database`.

mitigations.summary: Require authenticated, object-level authorization for customer reads
mitigations.detail: Make `process:web-api` deny reads by default, authenticate every caller, and enforce server-side ownership or role checks for each customer record and field returned.

mitigations.summary: Minimize API response fields and detect enumeration
mitigations.detail: Return only fields needed for each operation, avoid returning payment-card data, and rate-limit and alert on record-enumeration patterns.
